newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holzmann - Transrapid to go ahead without builders.
newsitem.headline: Holzmann - Transrapid to go ahead without builders.

text.p: German construction group Holzmann AG said on Friday that the consortium set up to design and build the Transrapid rail project would continue without the partners from the construction industry.
Holzmann told Reuters that the Transrapid consortium considered the costs associated with the German firms Philipp Holzmann AG, Hochtief AG and Bilfinger+Berger AG were too high.
The three builders had seen no room to reduce costs to the extent demanded by the other partners in the consortium, Holzmann said.
A spokesman for Holzmann said: "We have been informed that the remaining partners in the consortium will take on the costs of the project themselves."

The construction costs in the nine-billion mark ($5.2 billion) project were too high for the other partners after changes in the marked-out route which the rail route would follow on the Hamburg-Berlin route, Holzmann said.

The project leader, steel and engineering group Thyssen AG said that the project would continue despite the building firms pulling out. It said the departure of the builders would better secure financing for the project.

The Transrapid project, which uses magnetic levitation technology, has come under criticism both as to whether there is sufficient demand for it in Germany and whether it can justify the six billion marks of state funding Bonn plans to offer for it.
